::: {.fbr}

::: {.fbr-step}
::: {.fbr-title}
Feedback to men: more positive on getting ahead, more negative on getting along
:::

```{=html}
<div class="fbm">
  <div class="fbm-panels">

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 1 · Trait words</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Traits used in psychology research to measure agency and communion, sorted by type (agentic or communal) and tone (positive or negative).</p>
      <div class="fbr-grid">
        <div></div>
        <div class="fbr-grid-head">Agentic</div>
        <div class="fbr-grid-head">Communal</div>
        <div class="fbr-grid-side">Positive</div>
        <div class="fbr-cell fbr-cell-tl">ambitious<br>competent<br>determined</div>
        <div class="fbr-cell fbr-cell-tr">caring<br>helpful<br>supportive</div>
        <div class="fbr-grid-side">Negative</div>
        <div class="fbr-cell fbr-cell-bl">passive<br>insecure<br>dependent</div>
        <div class="fbr-cell fbr-cell-br">detached<br>inconsiderate<br>unapproachable</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 2 · Create reference points for the traits</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Computers can’t understand words directly, so a language model (BERT) reads each trait in the same sentence and turns every word into a long list of numbers, an embedding.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        In the review, the manager described this person as <mark>ambitious</mark> <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <code>[0.71, −0.36, 0.15, …]</code>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">We then average the trait embeddings within each group. This gives four reference points:</p>
      <ol class="fbm-list">
        <li>Positive agency</li>
        <li>Negative agency</li>
        <li>Positive communion</li>
        <li>Negative communion</li>
      </ol>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 3 · Create embeddings for employee mentions</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Next, we turn to the feedback itself and do the same. BERT reads each sentence, and we keep the embedding of every word that refers to the employee, such as "she", "he", "you" or "your". These embeddings capture the context in which the employee is mentioned.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "<mark>She</mark> should be more confident when presenting to clients." <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <code>[0.18, 0.42, −0.09, …]</code>
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "<mark>He</mark> could involve his team more in decisions." <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <code>[0.64, −0.21, 0.33, …]</code>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-note">Example sentences, not from the data.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 4 · Compare with the reference points</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">We measure how close each employee mention is in meaning to the four reference points, using <a href="https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/cosine-similarity" target="_blank"><strong>cosine similarity</strong></a>. For each mention, this gives four scores, which we combine into two net scores:</p>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">
        <strong>Net agency</strong> <span class="fbm-arrow">=</span> positive agency − negative agency
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">
        <strong>Net communion</strong> <span class="fbm-arrow">=</span> positive communion − negative communion
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">A higher score means the mention is closer in meaning to positive than to negative traits.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 5 · Test for gender differences</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">We average the net scores of all employee mentions within each feedback entry, then run two tests:</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        <span class="fbm-label">Main test</span>
        Compare female and male employees, using multilevel models that also account for the manager’s gender.
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        <span class="fbm-label">Robustness check</span>
        Repeat the test using only mentions that are the same for women and men, such as “you” and “your”. This rules out that “he” and “she” simply differ as words.
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 6 · Result</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Compared to feedback to women, feedback to men is more positive on getting ahead (agency) and less positive on getting along (communion).</p>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">
        <strong>Net agency:</strong> higher for men (β = 0.13, 95% CI [0.11, 0.16])
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">
        <strong>Net communion:</strong> lower for men (β = −0.19, 95% CI [−0.21, −0.16])
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">The differences are small, hold for gender-neutral mentions, and do not depend on the manager's gender.</p>
      <p class="fbm-note">"Positive" and "negative" refer to closeness to positive or negative traits, not to praise or criticism.</p>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="fbm-slider">
    <input type="range" min="1" max="6" step="1" value="1" aria-label="Method step">
    <div class="fbm-labels">
      <span>Traits</span><span>Reference points</span><span>Mentions</span><span>Net scores</span><span>Analysis</span><span>Result</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.fbr-step}
::: {.fbr-title}
Women are told to be more confident, men what to improve
:::

```{=html}
<div class="fbm">
  <div class="fbm-panels">

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 1 · Find the employee</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">In every sentence, the words referring to the employee are located: "she", "he", "you", "your" or the employee's (anonymised) name.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "<mark>She</mark> should feel more confident when presenting."
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "<mark>He</mark> can improve his planning."
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-note">Example sentences, not from the data.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 2 · Read the grammar</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">A transformer-based grammar parser (spaCy) finds the words that describe the employee: <strong>adjectives</strong> about them and <strong>verbs</strong> they are the subject or object of.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "She should <mark>feel</mark> more <mark>confident</mark> when presenting."
        <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> verb: <em>feel</em> · adjective: <em>confident</em>
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "He can <mark>improve</mark> his planning."
        <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> verb: <em>improve</em>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 3 · Standardise the words</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Each word is reduced to its base form, so variants count as one word.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        feels, feeling, felt <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <em>feel</em>
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        improves, improving, improved <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <em>improve</em>
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        leads, leading, led <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <em>lead</em>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">Spelling errors are corrected, and words used fewer than 10 times are left out.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        comunicate <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <em>communicate</em>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 4 · Find the distinctive words</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">For each word, a statistical method (weighted log-odds) compares how often it appears in feedback to women and to men. It corrects for how common each word is, so rare words don't look more distinctive than they are.</p>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result fbm-women">
        <strong>Positive score</strong> <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> more typical of feedback to women
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result fbm-men">
        <strong>Negative score</strong> <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> more typical of feedback to men
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 5 · Result: feedback to women</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Compared to feedback to men, feedback to women more often addresses confidence, feelings and encouragement.</p>
      <p class="lo-head">Most distinctive words for women</p>
      <div class="lo-list">
        <div class="lo-item fbm-result">
          <span class="lo-rank">1</span>
          <div class="lo-body">
            <span class="lo-word">confident</span>
            <span class="lo-ex">"She should be more <mark>confident</mark> when speaking with clients."</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="lo-item fbm-result">
          <span class="lo-rank">2</span>
          <div class="lo-body">
            <span class="lo-word">feel</span>
            <span class="lo-ex">"You will <mark>feel</mark> more at ease once you know the process."</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="lo-item fbm-result">
          <span class="lo-rank">3</span>
          <div class="lo-body">
            <span class="lo-word">encourage</span>
            <span class="lo-ex">"I <mark>encourage</mark> her to share her ideas in meetings."</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-note">Ranked from most to least distinctive.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 6 · Result: feedback to men</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Compared to feedback to women, feedback to men more often addresses what he should improve or needs to change.</p>
      <p class="lo-head">Most distinctive words for men</p>
      <div class="lo-list">
        <div class="lo-item fbm-result">
          <span class="lo-rank">1</span>
          <div class="lo-body">
            <span class="lo-word">improve</span>
            <span class="lo-ex">"He can <mark>improve</mark> how he plans his week."</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="lo-item fbm-result">
          <span class="lo-rank">2</span>
          <div class="lo-body">
            <span class="lo-word">need</span>
            <span class="lo-ex">"He <mark>needs</mark> to update the team more often."</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="lo-item fbm-result">
          <span class="lo-rank">3</span>
          <div class="lo-body">
            <span class="lo-word">tend</span>
            <span class="lo-ex">"You <mark>tend</mark> to take on too many tasks at once."</span>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-note">Ranked from most to least distinctive.</p>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="fbm-slider">
    <input type="range" min="1" max="6" step="1" value="1" aria-label="Method step">
    <div class="fbm-labels">
      <span>Employee</span><span>Grammar</span><span>Standardise</span><span>Compare</span><span>Women</span><span>Men</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.fbr-step}
::: {.fbr-title}
Women get kind words, but not always a high score
:::

```{=html}
<div class="fbm">
  <div class="fbm-panels">

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 1 · Prepare the feedback</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">We use feedback on the employee's development and remove someentries.</p>
      <div class="fbm-flow" style="margin-top: 1rem;">
        <div class="fbm-flow-step fbm-result">≈ 59,000 feedback entries</div>
        <div class="fbm-flow-step fbm-flow-out fbm-result"><span class="fbm-split-icon">✕</span> Non-English entries</div>
        <div class="fbm-flow-step fbm-flow-out fbm-result"><span class="fbm-split-icon">✕</span> Gender unknown or non-binary</div>
        <div class="fbm-flow-step fbm-flow-out fbm-result"><span class="fbm-split-icon">✕</span> No mention of the employee</div>
        <div class="fbm-flow-step fbm-flow-main fbm-result">≈ 35,000 feedback entries</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 2 · Break into sentences</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Each entry is split into sentences, and sentences with fewer than five words are left out.</p>
      <div class="fbm-split">
        <div class="fbm-split-entry fbm-result" style="text-align: left; background: #F8F9FA; color: #343A40; border: 1px solid #E6E6EA;">"She leads the team well. Her reports are always on time. See further above."</div>
        <div class="fbm-split-arrow">↓</div>
        <div class="fbm-split-sent fbm-kept fbm-result"><span class="fbm-split-icon">✓</span>She leads the team well.</div>
        <div class="fbm-split-sent fbm-kept fbm-result"><span class="fbm-split-icon">✓</span>Her reports are always on time.</div>
        <div class="fbm-split-sent fbm-dropped fbm-result"><span class="fbm-split-icon">✕</span>See further above.<span class="fbm-split-tag">too short</span></div>
        <div class="fbm-split-arrow">↓</div>
        <div class="fbm-split-entry fbm-result"><strong>≈ 170,000 sentences</strong> in total</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 3 · Measure the sentiment</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">A language model (<a href="https://huggingface.co/cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest" target="_blank"><strong>RoBERTa</strong></a>) reads each sentence and gives three scores: how likely it is to be positive, neutral or negative.</p>
      <div class="fbm-sent">
        <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">"She has grown a lot as a project lead this year."</div>
        <div class="fbm-scores">
          <span class="fbm-score fbm-score-pos">positive 0.97</span><span class="fbm-score">neutral 0.03</span><span class="fbm-score">negative 0.00</span>
        </div>
        <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">"Your updates to the team are often late."</div>
        <div class="fbm-scores">
          <span class="fbm-score">positive 0.02</span><span class="fbm-score">neutral 0.27</span><span class="fbm-score fbm-score-neg">negative 0.71</span>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text" style="margin-top: 0.9rem;">The model was not trained on workplace feedback, so it was tested first. On 198 test sentences, the model and a researcher gave the same label 90% of the time.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 4 · One score per feedback entry</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Each sentence gets one sentiment score: the positive score minus the negative score. Scores range from −1 (very negative) to +1 (very positive).</p>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        <span class="fbm-label">Positive example</span>
        0.97 − 0.00 <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <strong>+0.97</strong>
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        <span class="fbm-label">Negative example</span>
        0.02 − 0.71 <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> <strong>−0.69</strong>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">The scores of all sentences in an entry are then averaged, giving one score per entry.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 5 · Add the performance ratings</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Besides the written feedback, managers can give a performance rating from 1 to 4. About 19,000 entries have both.</p>
      <div class="fbm-scores" style="justify-content: center; margin: 0.6rem 0 0.9rem;">
        <span class="fbm-score">1 · lowest</span><span class="fbm-score">2</span><span class="fbm-score">3</span><span class="fbm-score">4 · highest</span>
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">This shows whether more positive feedback goes together with a higher rating.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 6 · Result</p>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">
        <span class="fbm-label">1 · Sentiment</span>
        Feedback to women is slightly more positive than feedback to men.<br>
        <strong>Sentiment score:</strong> lower for men (β = −0.10, 95% CI [−0.12, −0.07])
      </div>
      <div class="fbm-example fbm-result">
        <span class="fbm-label">2 · Sentiment and rating</span>
        For both women and men, more positive feedback goes with a higher rating, but the link is weaker for women.<br>
        <strong>Link with rating:</strong> stronger for men (β = 0.03, 95% CI [0.01, 0.06])
      </div>
      <p class="fbm-text">Both differences are small.</p>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="fbm-slider">
    <input type="range" min="1" max="6" step="1" value="1" aria-label="Method step">
    <div class="fbm-labels">
      <span>Feedback</span><span>Sentences</span><span>Sentiment</span><span>Score</span><span>Ratings</span><span>Result</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
:::


::: {.fbr-step}
::: {.fbr-title}
Female managers write longer and warmer feedback, especially at first
:::

```{=html}
<div class="fbm">
  <div class="fbm-panels">

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 1 · Compare the writers</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Here the focus is on <strong>who writes</strong> the feedback: female or male managers. The analysis takes the employee's gender into account, so the two effects are not mixed up.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 2 · Measure the length</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">A language-processing tool (spaCy) counts the words in each piece of feedback, and the average length is compared between female and male managers.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="fbm-panel">
      <p class="fbm-step-title">Step 3 · Measure the warmth</p>
      <p class="fbm-text">Two language models read every sentence:</p>

        <li><strong>Sentiment</strong> (RoBERTa): how positive or negative the feedback is</li>
        <li><strong>Emotions</strong> (GoEmotions): which of 28 emotions it expresses, such as caring or admiration</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="fbm-example">
        "I want to support you as you grow into this role." <span class="fbm-arrow">→</span> positive · caring

  </div>

</div>
```

:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  // ── Findings: one finding at a time, with Previous / Next and dots ──────────
  function setupFindings(root) {
    const steps = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll(':scope > .fbr-step'));
    if (!steps.length) return;
    let current = 0;

    const counter = document.createElement('div');
    counter.className = 'fbr-counter';
    root.insertBefore(counter, root.firstChild);

    const nav = document.createElement('div');
    nav.className = 'fbr-nav';
    const prev = document.createElement('button');
    prev.type = 'button'; prev.className = 'fbr-btn'; prev.textContent = '← Previous';
    const dots = document.createElement('div');
    dots.className = 'fbr-dots';
    const next = document.createElement('button');
    next.type = 'button'; next.className = 'fbr-btn'; next.textContent = 'Next →';
    steps.forEach(function (_, i) {
      const dot = document.createElement('button');
      dot.type = 'button'; dot.className = 'fbr-dot';
      dot.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Finding ' + (i + 1));
      dot.addEventListener('click', function () { show(i); });
      dots.appendChild(dot);
    });
    nav.appendChild(prev); nav.appendChild(dots); nav.appendChild(next);
    root.appendChild(nav);

    function show(i) {
      current = i;
      steps.forEach(function (s, j) { s.style.display = j === i ? '' : 'none'; });
      counter.textContent = 'Finding ' + (i + 1) + ' of ' + steps.length;
      prev.disabled = i === 0;
      next.disabled = i === steps.length - 1;
      dots.querySelectorAll('.fbr-dot').forEach(function (d, j) { d.classList.toggle('active', j === i); });
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));   // lets charts in a newly shown step resize
    }
    prev.addEventListener('click', function () { if (current > 0) show(current - 1); });
    next.addEventListener('click', function () { if (current < steps.length - 1) show(current + 1); });
    show(0);
  }

  // ── Method sliders: one method step at a time ───────────────────────────────
  function setupSlider(root) {
    const panels = root.querySelectorAll('.fbm-panel');
    const slider = root.querySelector('input[type=range]');
    const labels = root.querySelectorAll('.fbm-labels span');
    // Tell the CSS how many labels there are, so each label gets an equal share of space
    const labelRow = root.querySelector('.fbm-labels');
    if (labelRow) labelRow.style.setProperty('--n', labels.length);
    // Place each middle label so its centre sits under its slider stop
    labels.forEach(function (l, i) {
      if (i === 0 || i === labels.length - 1) return;
      const f = i / (labels.length - 1);
      l.style.left = 'calc(8px + ' + f + ' * (100% - 16px))';
    });
    function show(n) {
      panels.forEach(function (p, i) { p.style.display = (i === n - 1) ? 'block' : 'none'; });
      labels.forEach(function (l, i) { l.classList.toggle('active', i === n - 1); });
      slider.value = n;
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));
    }
    slider.addEventListener('input', function () { show(Number(slider.value)); });
    labels.forEach(function (l, i) { l.addEventListener('click', function () { show(i + 1); }); });
    show(1);
  }

  function init() {
    document.querySelectorAll('.fbm').forEach(setupSlider);
    document.querySelectorAll('.fbr').forEach(setupFindings);
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
  else init();
})();
</script>
```
